title: Pump System Units And Measurements
description: A draft first lesson for the Smart Pump Systems masterclass focused on explicit SI-unit measurement language.
learningOutcomes: Match pressure, flow, temperature, power, and time to their expected SI units.
Explain why ambiguous units must be resolved before calculation or diagnosis.

blocks.text: This first Smart Pump Systems lesson establishes the measurement language used before pressure, flow, pump curves, monitoring data, or fault diagnosis are introduced.
Students should be able to read a numeric measurement and recognise that engineering quantities require stated units.

By the end of the lesson, students should identify pump-system measurement quantities, match them to expected SI units, and explain why ambiguous units must be resolved before calculation or diagnosis.
Smart pump monitoring depends on measurement channels that state quantity, value, unit, and context; without those four pieces, later calculations and diagnosis can be misleading.

blocks.definition: A named signal or reading used to represent one measured quantity in the pump-system learning context.
The unit expected internally by Industrial Learn calculation and simulation functions for the relevant quantity.

blocks.title: Pump measurement row
blocks.altText: A pump measurement row shows quantity, value, unit, and context as separate required fields.
blocks.description: A usable pump-system reading needs a quantity label, numeric value, unit, and context before it is used for calculation or diagnosis.
blocks.caption: Measurement readiness diagram for Smart Pump Systems.

blocks.text: The first review step for any pump-system measurement is to identify the measured quantity, the numeric value, the unit, and the measurement context.
This lesson checks measurement readiness only and does not perform pump sizing, pump selection, or fault diagnosis.

blocks.note: This lesson introduces expected SI units but does not add a new engineering equation.

blocks.title: Check a pump measurement row
given: Context: discharge pressure reading in a training dataset

steps.label: Identify the quantity
steps.explanation: Pressure is the measured quantity, so the expected internal unit is pascal.

steps.label: Check the unit
steps.explanation: The stated unit matches the expected SI unit for pressure.

steps.label: Check context
steps.explanation: The reading has enough context for a later reviewed lesson to decide how it may be used.

blocks.result: Measurement row is ready for later reviewed interpretation.
blocks.interpretation: The row is not a diagnosis by itself; it is only a complete measurement record.

blocks.text: Planned simulation: students will classify pump-system measurement rows as ready, incomplete, or unsafe for diagnosis. The simulation is not implemented in this lesson task.

blocks.title: Ambiguous measurement unit
symptoms: A pump-system reading is recorded without a unit or with a non-SI unit.
blocks.safeResponse: Do not use the reading for diagnosis until the unit and conversion evidence are confirmed.

blocks.title: Real pump-system measurements
blocks.text: This training lesson does not authorise students to inspect, operate, adjust, or troubleshoot real pump equipment.

blocks.prompt: Which information must be present before a pump-system reading is ready for later calculation or diagnosis?

options.text: Only a number and a chart colour

blocks.answerExplanation: A usable measurement row needs the measured quantity, numeric value, unit, and context.

blocks.text: Smart pump learning starts with explicit measurement records. A reading is not ready for calculation or diagnosis until quantity, value, unit, and context are known.

blocks.note: NIST SP 330-2019, tables 4, 5, and 7, supports the SI names, symbols, and prefixes used in this draft.

The U.S. Department of Energy Pump Sourcebook, pages 56 to 60, supports the measurement-context and measurement-quality discussion. It does not establish equipment-specific limits or diagnostic thresholds.
